short: The name Mauri comes from the Mauritanian or Moorish people, the native population of Mauretania, which is in Northwest Africa. The Mauri by Strabo, who wrote in the early 1st century, is a local name that was also adopted in Latin, while he cites the same nation's Greek name as the Mauretania. The name Mauri as a tribal confederation or common ethnic designation probably therefore corresponds roughly to the people known in earlier history as the Numidians. There is also a theory that by this time the given title, used in the Roman army, did not designate an ethnicity but a particular type of military unit, but what type of unit, we can only speculate. Auxilia (latin) - an auxiliary unit of the Roman army.  There is a strong opinion that auxilia units consisted of barbarians-volunteers (primarily Germanic). Vegetius directly mentions that the legions were composed of Roman citizens, and the auxilia of barbarians. About the internal organisation of the auxilia nothing is definitely known, but most likely, the structure of these units in the 4th century was no different from the legions. While the legions were composed of forcefully conscripted Romanised barbarians who lived on the territory of the Empire, in the auxilia served mainly volunteers from the Germanic tribes beyond the Rhine. Such system led to the fact that the auxiliaries became superior to the legionnaires in terms of their combat qualities.
history: In the face of an increasing number of barbarian incursions, the effective defence of Rome’s now-sprawling territory became a serious problem in the 4th century AD. The Emperor Constantine’s controversial solution was to divide the army into two halves. 'Limitanei', literally ‘the men on the limes’ or 'borders', were frontier garrison troops intended to pin down an invading force until the full-time 'comitatenses', the late-Roman equivalent of the traditional Legionaries, could arrive to deal with the situation decisively. Although well-equipped, limitanei were generally considered by all to be second-class warriors. This was possibly because they were often part-time soldiers who had been encouraged to settle and farm the land around their outposts in exchange for policing the Empire's borders.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
